findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are never upgraded with the Clients schema
findings.body: `init` returns as soon as an admin-permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore retain only the previously-created Users resource/scopes and never receive the Clients all-resource or the new `configure`, `map-roles-client-scope`, and `map-roles-composite` scopes. Creating a Clients permission in such a realm will fail when `getOrCreateResource` cannot find its scopes, and global client permissions cannot be evaluated because the Clients resource is absent. Schema initialization needs an idempotent upgrade path that creates missing scopes and resource-type resources for an existing client.

findings.title: V2 client role-mapping checks drop the manage-clients administrator bypass
findings.body: `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` only evaluate a V2 resource permission. Unlike the existing client evaluator behavior, they do not allow a caller holding the built-in `manage-clients` role. Since `MgmtPermissionsV2` is selected globally whenever the V2 feature is enabled, realm administrators with `manage-clients` will be forbidden from assigning client roles or managing composite/client-scope role mappings unless separate V2 policies are created. Preserve the built-in admin-role bypass (and any existing transitive manage behavior) before performing the V2 scope evaluation.

findings.title: Client deletion either invokes an unsupported V2 operation or leaves V2 permission data orphaned
findings.body: The deletion listener is now gated on the old `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature, but `management()` selects `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled. If both features are enabled, deleting a client calls `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled`, which always throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (line 193), potentially failing the deletion event. If V2 alone is enabled, the listener is skipped, so client-specific Clients resources and policies stored on the realm admin-permissions client are never removed when the target client is deleted. Implement V2-aware cleanup for client removal rather than routing it through the unsupported legacy permission-management method.
